surprises_or_findings:
1. The 4-test regression from 1cb58a5 is a textbook Bug Fix Sequence § 3 violation. The fix commit acknowledged the issue ('This is a design bug in ehp.13 / ehp.7 (precondition table coverage). Tracked under poh.3 for the proper fix.') AND named the proper follow-on bead — but shipped the broken state anyway. The review found this empirically by running `npx jest` rather than trusting builder-marker test-pass claims; this is the right shape per marker-protocol § 1 ('Write marker LAST + verify... never trust the close return code alone').

2. The 1cb58a5 fix is operationally correct (it unblocked review-wave dispatch which was previously refused with NO_WAVE_BEADS for the legitimate post-close case). The regression is purely on the OPPOSITE protection (refusing review-wave for the niii reviewer-4-wave-4-redundant case where all wave beads are STILL closed but the review is firing redundantly because the wave's already been reviewed). Both protections are needed; v1's library structure (ACTIONS_REQUIRING_WAVE_BEADS as a single set) cannot disambiguate them. The proper fix (already tracked under poh.3) is a new 'wave-N beads of ANY status exist' predicate.

3. ehp.10's marker says 'deviations_from_ac: None' but the bead's Out clause was unambiguously violated (modified existing agent-launcher-marker-routing.test.ts despite explicit prohibition). The deviation is ACCEPT-able for the reasons documented in the o2s bug (the Out clause was infeasible — adding a precondition gate to dispatchChainAction breaks every existing kvn test unless they get a bead-status mock that requires top-level test-file modification). But the marker should have surfaced it. This is the second-line defense (reviewer) catching a builder marker discipline gap, exactly what surfacing-protocol § 2.3 failure mode 3 describes.

4. ehp.7's 'Goodbye-without-marker' first dispatch (per close reason: 'ehp.7 had a silent failure (Goodbye-without-marker) on first dispatch at 23:37; required re-dispatch via start-wave 4 (after fixing route.ts cross-repo + plan-path issues at 32c76b8 / 2c2cab5 + symlink workaround). Second builder ran cleanly + self-committed.') is a process issue tracked under poh.1, not a Wave-4 code defect. The second-builder commit (e11bc89) landed clean code and a proper marker. Recorded for completeness.

5. Wave-4 review caught two issues that Wave-3 review missed: (a) the review-wave inclusion in ACTIONS_REQUIRING_WAVE_BEADS that ehp.13's Wave-3 review actually praised as 'review-wave carries both NO_WAVE_BEADS + ALL_WAVE_BEADS_CLOSED per ehp.7 contract' — turning out to be the wrong contract; (b) the cross-repo epic-resolution gap in ehp.11's checkPreconditionsOrRefuse helper (originally hardcoded fleetCorePath; fixed in 32c76b8). Both surfaced empirically during Wave-4 dispatch attempts, NOT during the Wave-3 review pass. Suggests Wave reviews should include an end-to-end dispatch smoke test for the actions the wave gates.
